18b381d68aea685b851e.title: Appointment Sales Specialist
18b381d68aea685b851e.description:
**Are you a closer who thrives on turning interest into commitment?**  
We’re not hiring a receptionist or a customer service rep. We’re hiring a **phone-based sales professional** who understands that every call is an opportunity to help someone take the next step—and to grow revenue by doing it the right way.

The Role

As our **Appointment Sales Specialist**, you’ll respond to inbound calls/web leads and run outbound follow-up for people who already raised their hand. Your goal is simple:

**Convert qualified leads into scheduled appointments with a paid reservation deposit.**

This is a consultative sales role. You’ll listen, diagnose the real barrier, communicate our value clearly, and handle objections professionally—without being pushy.

What You’ll Do

* **Convert inbound leads:** Turn calls and form submissions into booked appointments.
* **Secure reservation deposits:** Confidently collect deposits over the phone in accordance with our policy to protect show rates.
* **Outbound follow-up:** Re-engage warm leads who didn’t schedule (no cold calling).
* **Handle objections:** Cost, timing, “need to think about it,” spouse approval, fear/uncertainty—your job is to lead the conversation to a decision.
* **Own the pipeline:** Keep CRM notes clean, follow-ups tight, and ensure no lead falls through the cracks.
* **Improve through coaching:** You’ll be recorded/role-played/coached to continuously improve conversion and show rate.

Who You Are

* **A proven closer:** You’re comfortable asking for payment on the phone, and you do it professionally.
* **High empathy + high standards:** You build rapport fast *and* you move the conversation to commitment.
* **Process-driven:** You follow a script, use a CRM correctly, and you don’t “wing it.”
* **Experienced:** 2+ years in phone sales, enrollment, inside sales, or appointment setting (healthcare is a plus).

How We Measure Success

* **Lead-to-appointment conversion rate**
* **Deposit collection rate**
* **Show rate on booked appointments**
* **Speed-to-lead + follow-up completion**
* **Pipeline cleanliness (no stale leads)**

Compensation

* **Base:** $25–$30/hour
* **Remote:** Work from home (quiet environment, reliable internet, headset required)
* **Schedule:** Must be available during **Pacific Time business hours** (specific shifts TBD)

Pay: $25.00 - $30.00 per hour

Benefits:

* Work from home

Application Question(s):

* In your most recent phone sales or appointment-setting role, how many dials did you make per day, how many appointments did you set per week, and what was your show rate? Give real numbers.

Work Location: Remote

$60,000 - $65,000 yearly

Applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy), age, sexual orientation, national origin, marital status, parental status, ancestry, disability, gender identity, veteran status, genetic information, other distinguishing characteristics of diversity and inclusion, or any other protected status. 8af5691864a8ceb56570.title: Revenue Operations Specialist
8af5691864a8ceb56570.description:
**About The Princeton Review**

The Princeton Review is a leading tutoring, test prep, and college admission services company. Every year, it helps millions of college- and graduate school–bound students achieve their education and career goals through online and in-person courses delivered by a network of more than 4,000 teachers and tutors, online resources, and its more than 150 print and digital books published by Penguin Random House. The company's Tutor.com brand is one of the largest online tutoring services in the U.S. It comprises a community of thousands of tutors who have delivered more than 22 million one-to-one tutoring sessions. The Princeton Review is headquartered in New York, NY. Follow the company on LinkedIn, YouTube and Instagram.

**About the Position**

We're looking for a detail-obsessed, quick-learning Revenue Operations Specialist to join our remote team and keep our revenue data accurate, visible, and actionable. In this role, you'll track and forecast revenue across accounts, reconcile records with Accounting, and manage revenue data in Salesforce. You'll also guide Sales and Customer Success toward the highest-priority accounts to close each month.

Day to day, you'll write Standard Operating Procedures, audit internal systems, and work with teams across the company (Sales, Marketing, Legal, Accounts Receivable, and senior leadership) to resolve invoicing questions quickly and accurately. You'll also take on special projects, including building a new invoicing process in Salesforce, managing non-standard contract compliance, serving as the Sales and Marketing liaison on lead list management and CCPA compliance, and helping launch new Sales Enablement tools such as a Sales Playbook on SharePoint.

**What You'll Do**

* Identify and track all potential revenue earnings for each account, report to Leadership weekly, and reconcile records with Accounting monthly.
* Guide the Sales and Customer Success teams to maximize impact on revenue by identifying high priority accounts to close each month.
* Design and write Standard Operating Procedures when needed to improve accuracy, efficiency, and usability for internal teams.
* Coordinate with multiple internal teams to ensure quick and accurate response to customer inquiries regarding invoicing.
* Verify and input sales credits and debits into our internal tools to guarantee customer account balances as displayed accessible and accurate for our clients.
* Audit data entries and program statuses in our internal systems.
* Effectively communicate system needs to Salesforce Administrator and Sales Operations leadership to support design of technological tools that will improve workflow for business unit.
* Design and maintain a new invoicing process that bridges information in our proprietary Customer Service Tool and Salesforce.
* Manage non-standard contract compliance and reporting, using Claude AI and Salesforce to identify and track requirements.
* Serve as a liaison between Sales and Marketing regarding lead list management and sales follow-through.
* Write, build, and maintain the Sales Playbook on SharePoint.

**Who You Are**

* 3-5 years of Sales Operations, Revenue Operations, or Sales experience, preferably in B2B SaaS
* Extremely detail oriented, prone to checking every last number and data point
* Ability to quickly learn new concepts and systems.
* Adept at using Excel for data entry, data preparation and some data analysis: pivot tables, vlookups, sumifs are all important to this position
* Knowledgeable of general accounting principles related to deferred revenue calculations and reporting
* Comfortable running reports in Salesforce Lightning and navigating the Salesforce environment.
* SharePoint experience preferred
* Comfortable using AI tools such as Claude to improve efficiencies in workflow
* Ability to interface professionally and effectively with many personality types from various departments including senior management, sales and service, marketing, legal team, and accounts receivables
* Work quickly, independently and remotely with an ability to adapt to changes in priority as needed
* Collaborate with, support, and lean on teammates when needed
* Willing to put in extra time during our busiest season with the understanding that flexibility will be reciprocated

*The Princeton Review is an equal employment opportunity employer. The Princeton Review's policy is not to discriminate against any applicant or employee based on, and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to, race, color, religion, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, marital status, disability, military status, genetic information, or any other basis protected by applicable law. The Princeton Review also prohibits harassment of applicants or employees based on any of these protected categories. It is also The Princeton Review's policy to comply with all applicable laws respecting consideration of unemployment status in making hiring decisions.*

2ed23031aaeb8f9c618d.title: Senior Global Partner Specialist - USA
2ed23031aaeb8f9c618d.description:
Storyblok is a headless CMS that enables marketers and developers to create with joy and publish with confidence. It empowers you to deliver structured and consistent content everywhere: websites, apps, AI search, and beyond.

Legendary brands like Virgin Media O2, Oatly, and TomTom use Storyblok to make a bigger, faster market impact.

  

**WHAT IS IN IT FOR YOU**

You will be joining a growing company where you can contribute to many "firsts". Plus these benefits:

* Monthly remote work stipend (home internet costs, electricity). Home office equipment package right at the start (laptop, keyboard, monitor…)
* Home office equipment upgrade (furniture, ear plugs …) or membership to a local co-working space after your onboarding
* Sick leave benefit, parental leave and 25 days of annual leave plus your local national holidays
* Personal development fund for courses, books, conferences, and material
* The annual international team-building trip, quarterly and monthly online get-togethers
* As a fully remote company, with work-life balance at its core, you'll enjoy flexible schedules
* An international team that loves to have fun at work and works hard together to accomplish shared goals

**Job Summary**
---------------

The Senior Global Partner Specialist owns the growth and commercial performance of Storyblok's global Longtail partner ecosystem, including New, Nurturing, and Emerging partners of all sizes.

This role develops and delivers scalable programs that enable partners, increase partner-sourced and partner-influenced revenue, and move partners through the lifecycle from onboarding to sustained commercial activity. Operating primarily through one-to-many engagement, automation, self-service, and data-driven segmentation, the role ensures Storyblok can support and grow a broad partner base efficiently. The role also identifies practical opportunities to use AI and emerging technologies to improve partner experience, efficiency, and scale.

The Senior Global Partner Specialist identifies high-potential Longtail partners that are ready to progress into the Focused segment and works cross-functionally to continuously improve Storyblok's global partner growth model.

**Essential Job Functions**
---------------------------

* Own and continuously improve the global growth strategy and engagement model for New, Nurturing, and Emerging partners.
* Drive partner-sourced and partner-influenced pipeline and revenue across the Longtail partner ecosystem.
* Design and deliver scalable one-to-many programs that support partner activation, enablement, engagement, and commercial growth.
* Manage partner lifecycle communications and campaigns across relevant channels and partner cohorts.
* Use partner data and performance insights to improve segmentation, prioritization, lifecycle progression, and program effectiveness.
* Identify barriers to partner growth and lead cross-functional initiatives to improve the partner experience and commercial outcomes.
* Own the process for identifying, assessing, and recommending high-potential Longtail partners for progression into the Focused segment.
* Collaborate with Partner Management, Sales, Marketing, Partner Enablement, Solutions Engineering, Developer Experience, and Operations to deliver a connected partner journey.
* Identify opportunities to use AI and automation to reduce repetitive work, improve partner self-service, and scale partner engagement while preserving human involvement for high-value commercial and strategic moments.
* Define and monitor success measures, share insights with Partner Leadership, and continuously optimize programs based on measurable outcomes.

**Education and Experience**
----------------------------

* 4-5 years of relevant experience in partnerships, channel management, partner growth, partner programs, business development, revenue programs, or a related SaaS environment.
* Demonstrated experience owning complex programs or business initiatives with measurable commercial outcomes.
* Experience managing or influencing a large portfolio of partners, customers, or accounts through scalable programs.
* Strong understanding of SaaS sales cycles, partner ecosystems, and lifecycle or growth programs.
* Strong analytical skills and experience using CRM, PRM, engagement, enablement, and pipeline data to guide decisions.
* Experience working globally and cross-functionally with commercial, marketing, enablement, operational, and technical stakeholders.
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English.
* Demonstrated ability to work independently and lead complex initiatives with limited oversight.

**Professional Competencies**
-----------------------------

* **Commercial orientation:** Connects partner activity to pipeline and revenue and prioritizes work based on business impact.
* **Program strategy and management:** Translates strategic objectives into scalable programs and leads complex initiatives from concept through optimization.
* **One-to-many partner management:** Creates relevant partner experiences across a large portfolio without relying on continuous individual account management.
* **Lifecycle, segmentation, and prioritization:** Uses partner maturity, behavior, capability, and commercial signals to guide engagement and investment.
* **Analytical problem solving:** Uses qualitative and quantitative insights to diagnose challenges and develop effective solutions.
* **Cross-functional leadership:** Aligns stakeholders across functions and influences decisions without relying on direct authority.
* **Technology and automation mindset:** Identifies practical opportunities to use automation, AI, and digital tools to improve partner experience, operational efficiency, and program scalability.
* **Autonomy and ownership:** Takes accountability for outcomes and makes sound decisions in an evolving, global environment.

**Key Success Measures**
------------------------

* Partner-sourced and partner-influenced pipeline and revenue from Longtail partners
* Growth in commercially active partners and first and repeat opportunity generation
* Progression across partner lifecycle stages
* Effectiveness of one-to-many partner programs and communications
* Number and quality of partners progressed from Longtail to Focused
* Growth in partner productivity without proportional growth in manual management effort
  

***U.S. Base Salary Range: $97,000 - $132,000***

We consider many factors when it comes to compensation, such as the scope of the role, job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training. Our base salary ranges are determined by job and job level and are benchmarked to relevant location and industry data. The range displayed represents the target US base compensation range within which we are hiring for this role. For some roles Storyblok also offers a competitive commission structure.*

0006365346324c81055f.title: Program Manager, Onboarding + Training
0006365346324c81055f.description:
### **This is a remote role** **Position Details + Benefits**

* $85K base salary. We pay 100% of employee premiums for our base medical, dental, and vision plans

* Remote role. Travel up to four times per year to NYC or other ParentChild+ sites for training, professional development, and other program activities.

* 403(b) - 6% employer match! + FSA + HSA

* High accountability + high flexibility culture

### **About Us**

ParentChild+ is a national early childhood organization founded in 1965. We work with local partners across the country to help families support their children's early learning and prepare them for school. Our National Center provides training, resources, and support to the organizations delivering our programs in their communities.

We have two home visiting models:

* Family Model: Helps parents support their children's learning and development through play, books, and everyday interactions.

* Home-Based Child Care Model: Helps home-based child care providers create engaging learning environments for young children.

At each local site, Coordinators manage the program, train and supervise staff, and support program quality. Early Learning Specialists (ELSs) visit families or child care providers, using books, toys, and play to support children's learning and development.

### **Your Mission**

Your job is to coordinate and co-lead training opportunities for new ParentChild+ Family Model Coordinators and Home Visitors as they prepare to launch a new site. You'll also manage the process of helping new Family Model sites get started from initial planning through onboarding and training.

You'll work closely with our other National Center teams to make sure your training and onboarding run smoothly and that new sites have the support they need to succeed.

### **Responsibilities**

Facilitation, Coaching + Practice Support

* Lead two intensive, six-week training programs each year, along with smaller training sessions throughout the year. You'll train about 25 new Coordinators annually from partner organizations who are learning to bring the Family Model to their communities. Your manager and other trainers will help you prepare and lead these sessions.

* Work with your manager and other teams to prepare and lead training on assessments. You'll receive formal training to prepare you for these sessions, as needed.

* After training, you'll continue working with these Coordinators through a Community of Practice (CoP). You'll lead group meetings every two weeks for seven months, helping Coordinators solve problems, support their Home Visitors, and improve how they run their programs.

* Turn Family Model standards and findings from program evaluations into clear, practical guidance that Coordinators and sites can use in their daily work.

### **Program Management & Operations**

* Manage the New Coordinator Training Institute and Communities of Practice. Work with your manager to set training priorities, coordinate with other trainers, and make sure new Coordinators learn the skills and Family Model standards they need.

* Use program data, evaluation findings, participant feedback, and experience from local sites to identify training needs and improve future training.

* Build and improve administrative processes across departments for training, evaluation, and other activities involving local sites. Coordinate schedules, registration, communications, materials, and recordkeeping so responsibilities are clear and work runs smoothly.

* Maintain and update documents, training materials, and other resources shared with sites on the Staff Portal, working with other departments on updates and translations as needed.

* Develop and coordinate program eBlasts to share training opportunities, evaluation activities, program updates, and other important information with our network.

### **Site Startup + Onboarding**

* Develop and manage a clear, consistent process for helping new Family Model sites get started, working closely with other National Center teams.

* Coordinate the steps involved in opening a new site, including schedules, staff responsibilities, site orientation, and preparation for training. Make sure everyone understands what needs to happen and when.

* Track each new site's progress, identify problems or areas where additional support is needed, and work with State Directors and other teams to help sites get their programs up and running.

### **Qualifications**

* 5+ years' experience in early childhood or family support programs.

* Adult Learning + Facilitation: Experience developing and leading training for adults, including group discussions and activities. Experience with reflective supervision or coaching is a plus.

* Organization + Program Management: Strong organizational skills, including managing schedules, coordinating projects, and keeping multiple activities on track.

* Equitable Orientation: Commitment to strength-based, equity-centered, and culturally responsive practice.

* Technology: Comfortable using Microsoft Office, Zoom, and Management Information Systems (MIS).

### **Preferred Qualifications**

* You speak Spanish or another ParentChild+ priority language (e.g., Mandarin, Arabic, or Haitian Creole).

* Basic understanding of data analysis

### **What Success Looks Like in Your First Year**

* New Site Onboarding: Create and document a clear process for starting new sites, including responsibilities, timelines, and what sites need to have in place before launching. Test and improve the process as new sites come on board.

* Program Operations: Improve administrative processes that support work across departments, including site communications, eBlasts, and maintaining Staff Portal resources. Make sure responsibilities and timelines are clear.

* Training Management: Plan and manage two annual training institutes and their Communities of Practice. Keep training organized, meet deadlines, and improve processes to reduce administrative work.

* Training Delivery: Lead engaging training sessions that encourage discussion, reflection, and practical learning. Demonstrate strong facilitation skills through observation and positive participant feedback.

* Coaching + Practice Support: Build coaching skills through training and practice. Gradually take on more responsibility for coaching Coordinators and sites, with support from your manager.

* Training Improvement: Use participant feedback and program data to identify training needs and make a meaningful improvement to foundational training.

84c03bf8797a414eb0bb.description:
The **Communications & Analytics Coordinator** is a key member of the Corporate Communications team, supporting the execution and delivery of Corporate Communications initiatives across the Home Office. This role is responsible for the operational side of communications, including but not limited to scheduling, deployment, tracking, and coordination, ensuring all campaigns are executed efficiently and on time.

Working closely with the Corporate Communications Manager, this position supports email campaigns, internal communications, event communications, and engagement initiatives, while helping to improve visibility into performance and results. This role reports directly to the Corporate Communications Manager.

**CLASSIFICATION:** Salaried, Exempt

**LOCATION:** Remote (~1 day in the office per month), Philadelphia Region Preferred

* Execute and distribute communications across platforms such as ActiveCampaign and FranConnect, including newsletters, event promotions, organizational announcements, discussion board posts, and ad hoc campaigns in alignment with established corporate communications plans.
* Ensure accuracy, formatting quality, and adherence to brand voice and communications standards across all communications prior to distribution.
* Manage daily communications workflows and maintain the communications calendar to ensure timely execution and delivery of assigned campaigns.
* Maintain and update project statuses in project management software to support accurate tracking, visibility, and coordination across Marketing and Corporate Communications stakeholders.
* Collaborate with internal teams and subject matter experts to gather content, draft communications, coordinate design alignment, and fulfill communication requests under the direction of the Corporate Communications Manager.

* Manage and maintain distribution lists and audience segmentation to support accurate targeting and effective message delivery.
* Support execution of communication plans for key events, including pre-event promotions, reminders, and post-event follow-up communications, while tracking registration and engagement metrics.
* Plan and coordinate company-wide webinar communications plans, including promotional communications, intranet updates, logistical coordination, and day-of operational support.

* Provide internal feedback and recommendations to Corporate Communications leadership to improve workflow efficiency and address evolving communication needs.

It is not intended to be an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties, and skills required. Duties, responsibilities, and activities may be assigned or changed at any time. Additionally, this employer is an equal opportunity employer and will provide reasonable accommodations to qualified individuals with disabilities as required by law.

* Minimum of 1–3 years of experience in communications, marketing, or a related role.

Clinical Research Project Manager

**Contract | U.S. study start-up | Approximately four months with** possibility **for extension.**

A clinical research consulting firm is seeking an experienced Clinical Research Project Manager to lead U.S. start-up for a rare disease clinical trial. The engagement runs from study kick-off through activation of the first U.S. investigational site. You’ll own the start-up timeline, coordinate deliverables across teams, and make high-level operational decisions that affect study readiness and activation.

Responsibilities

* Lead day-to-day start-up activities, set priorities, and make decisions about sequencing work, resolving issues, and mitigating risks. Escalate decisions that require sponsor approval.
* Develop and coordinate review of the Project and Risk Management Plan, Quality Plan, Trial Master File (TMF) Plan, Monitoring Plan, Medical Monitoring Plan, and Data and Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB) Charter. Partner with Data Management on paper case report form (CRF) development. The scope includes one draft and one final version of each deliverable.
* Prepare and distribute the Investigator Site File (ISF) package for one U.S. site. Collect essential documents and track site readiness through activation.
* Develop a master site agreement template, tailor it for the U.S. site, and support negotiations through execution.
* Conduct one remote site qualification visit and prepare the report. Coordinate one on-site Site Initiation Visit (SIV), which the Clinical Research Associate (CRA) will conduct, including site staff training and reporting.
* Establish and maintain the electronic Trial Master File (eTMF), including folder structure, document naming conventions, and access controls.
* Prepare two study status reports covering progress, milestones, risks, and mitigation actions.
* Organize and participate in the internal team kick-off, a four-hour remote sponsor kick-off, a four-hour remote investigator meeting, and approximately 16 weekly sponsor calls. **Lead or join ad hoc calls** with the sponsor, site, and study team as needed to resolve urgent issues and make time-sensitive decisions.

Qualifications

* Clinical research project management experience with hands-on responsibility for U.S. study start-up and site activation.
* Demonstrated ability to make sound operational decisions, manage competing priorities, and escalate issues promptly.
* Experience managing start-up timelines, essential documents, eTMF activities, and cross-functional deliverables.
* Working knowledge of FDA clinical trial requirements and ICH Good Clinical Practice (GCP).
* Strong written communication, meeting facilitation, and risk management skills.
* Rare disease trial experience and current GCP training documentation preferred.

Confidentiality and authorization

The hiring organization, sponsor, and study identifiers are confidential. Study-specific details and materials may be shared once the required written permission is obtained and the candidate signs a Confidential Disclosure Agreement (CDA). Access to study documents and systems requires prior authorization.

**To apply**, submit your résumé through Indeed and include your earliest available start date and a brief example of a U.S. site activation you led.

Pay: Up to $55.00 per hour

Expected hours: 30.0 – 40.0 per week

Work Location: Remote

PHMC serves as both a direct service provider to individuals, families, and communities across the region and an intermediary agent—managing large-scale contracts, government and philanthropic partnerships, and multidisciplinary initiatives that require operational sophistication, strategic leadership, and deep mission alignment.

**COMPONENT:**

City

**DIVISION:**

Philadelphia Department of Public Health – Division of Reproductive, Adolescent, and Child Health

**LOCATION**:

300 East Hunting Park

**REPORTS TO:**

Clinical Director/Manager

**Schedule:**

Monday-to-Friday, 9 am to 5 pm

**FTE Status**-Full-Time

**Job Overview:**

ReACH is seeking a highly organized, detail-oriented, and dependable Administrative Program Coordinator to provide comprehensive administrative and operational support to the Philadelphia Sexual Assault Response Center (PSARC). PSARC provides trauma-informed, patient-centered forensic medical services to individuals who have experienced sexual assault. The Program Administrator plays an essential role in supporting the center’s mission by facilitating efficient daily operations, maintaining organizational systems, coordinating staff activities, and ensuring timely communication among internal and external stakeholders. The person in this position will serve as the primary administrative support to the Clinical Director/Manager and help coordinate the administrative functions needed to maintain a 24-hour sexual assault response program.

This position requires a high degree of professionalism, discretion, initiative, accountability, and the ability to independently manage competing administrative priorities.

**Responsibilities:**

* **Executive and Administrative Support.**

* Provide direct administrative support for daily program operations.
* Monitor designated administrative email accounts and ensure timely routing and follow-up of correspondence.
* Maintain organized electronic and physical filing systems for forensic medical records, District Attorney and private attorney legal requests, and witness subpoenas.
* Track assigned projects, deadlines, pending requests, and outstanding action items.
* Assist with preparing presentations, operational reports, meeting materials, program flyers, folders, and program updates.
* Maintain confidentiality regarding personnel, survivors, legal, and organizational information.

* **Assist with Staff Scheduling and Personnel Coordination**

* Coordinate and maintain the Sexual Assault Nurse Examiner (SANE) on-call schedule.
* Monitor scheduling gaps and promptly notify the Clinical Director of anticipated coverage concerns.
* Communicate with SANEs regarding scheduling requests, availability, meetings, training, and administrative announcements.
* Maintain administrative records of staff certifications, continuing education, mandatory training, and credential expiration dates.
* Maintain accurate staff contact lists, availability records, and scheduling documentation.
* Assist with onboarding new employees, including tracking required documentation, training completion, and orientation schedules.
* Track staff meeting attendance and required administrative submissions.

* **Program Operations and Office Management**

* Support the daily administrative operations of PSARC to promote efficiency, organization, and continuity of services.
* Maintain an inventory of office supplies, administrative materials, and designated program equipment.
* Coordinate supply requests, purchasing documentation, vendor communication, and delivery tracking.
* Maintain administrative logs, operational checklists, and equipment maintenance schedules.
* Assist with organizing workspaces and maintaining a professional, welcoming, and trauma-informed environment.
* Support the implementation and maintenance of program policies, procedures, forms, and operational workflows.
* Identify administrative inefficiencies and recommend improvements to the Clinical Director.

* **Data Collection, Reporting, and Quality Improvement**

* Assist with collecting, organizing, and maintaining program statistics and administrative performance data.
* Maintain tracking spreadsheets and databases for program activities, staffing, training, and operational metrics.
* Assist the Clinical Director with preparing monthly, quarterly, and annual reports.
* Track designated program performance indicators and administrative compliance requirements.
* Maintain accurate records for audits, program evaluations, and quality improvement initiatives.
* Monitor completion of assigned administrative corrective actions and provide status updates to the Clinical Director.
* Ensure that data collection and reporting activities comply with confidentiality and organizational requirements.

* **Medical Records and Legal Administrative Coordination**

* Maintain secure administrative tracking systems for medical records requests, subpoenas, and other legal correspondence.
* Forward requests to the appropriate legal or records department in accordance with established procedures.
* Monitor request status, document correspondence, and follow up on outstanding administrative actions.
* Assist with maintaining organized documentation related to evidence transfer and chain-of-custody administrative tracking, as authorized.
* Ensure all confidential records and communications are handled according to applicable privacy laws, organizational policies, and established procedures.

**Skills:**

* Ability to protect sensitive survivor, employee, and organizational information.
* Ability to provide compassionate, professional, and nonjudgmental assistance.
* Excellent organizational and time-management skills with the ability to prioritize tasks and manage multiple responsibilities.
* Ability to identify administrative challenges and recommend solutions.
* Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, particularly Word, Excel, and Outlook.
* Strong written and verbal communication skills.
* Ability to work independently and manage competing priorities.
* Ability to assist with budgets, invoices, purchasing, and expense tracking.
* Ability to recognize boundaries and refer sensitive matters to leadership.

**Experience:**

* At least two years of experience managing daily office operations and administrative functions
* Familiarity with trauma-informed and survivor-centered practices preferred
* Experience maintaining confidential records and sensitive information preferred

**Education Requirement:**

* Associate's or Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Office Management, Public Administration, Human Services, or a related field preferred.
* Equivalent education and relevant work experience may be considered.
* Additional training in confidentiality, trauma-informed practices, victim services, or nonprofit administration is desirable

Shaneita Goode: shaneita.goode@phila.gov (mailto:shaneita.goode@phila.gov)

If the answer to any of these questions is “Yes!”, then keep reading!

CorneaGen is a mission-driven company focused on advancing ocular care through meaningful innovations that transform patient lives while honoring every donor gift. Guided by our commitments to Trusted Tissue Stewardship, Exceptional Service, and Advancing Eye Care, we strive to make a lasting difference for patients, surgeons, partners, and the communities we serve. In support of this goal, we are looking for a Family Services Coordinator- Full Time to join our team.

**What does a Family Services Coordinator do?**

The **Family Services Coordinator** contributes to a dynamic industry which operates 24 hours a day, 7 days per week; serves as the point of contact regarding incoming referrals, coordinates specific functions of the donation program including receiving initial referrals and assessing/determining donor potential for CorneaGen and with all external donation partners, and directs recovery arrangements. The FSC is responsible for working with families to provide information regarding donation opportunities & obtaining authorization.

**JOB DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES**

**Job Location**

* This is a remote/work-from home position
* Shifts are composed of 12-hour increments (subject to change). Work hours will primarily include evenings and weekends.

**Referrals and Donor Screening**

* + Handles inbound and outbound communication with donation stakeholders such as hospitals/hospices/medical examiner offices/funeral homes and assesses suitability for eye donation
  + Captures all information timely, accurately, and completely within donor management software
  + Provides comprehensive medical screening of potential donors by effectively communicating with referral source personnel to determine suitability for eye recovery based on established guidelines
  + Discusses screening information and criteria applications with Family Services Director accordingly
  + Routinely provides feedback to appropriate chain of management regarding hospital education needs, community outreach opportunities, and development with donation partner agencies

**Donor Advocacy and Logistics**

* + Works in close collaboration with hospitals, team members, and Family Services Director to evaluate and determine the best time to offer families the opportunity for donation
  + Leads donation discussion with potential donor families or agents

acabbe7abd9498249bfe.title: Clinical TA Offer Coordinator
acabbe7abd9498249bfe.description:
POSITION PURPOSE

The Clinical TA Offer Coordinator manages the operational execution and quality of the provider offer process, from approved offer terms through document completion and accurate handoff. This role safeguards the candidate experience by coordinating offer documentation, electronic signatures, data accuracy, and risk-related follow-up across Talent Acquisition and its partners.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

* Offer Workflow Ownership. Coordinate the offer lifecycle for physicians and other clinical providers, including Letters of Intent (LOIs), Employment Agreements (EAs), Offer Letters (OLs), and independent contractor/1099 agreements, using approved terms, templates, and established approval pathways.
* Agreement Quality Control. Complete a documented pre-release review for consistency among approved offer terms, compensation and commencement details, employer/entity and practice information, candidate identifiers, effective dates, signature blocks, exhibits, and required supporting documents. Route discrepancies to the appropriate owner before release.
* Electronic Signature and Storage. Prepare and route documents through approved eSignature workflows; monitor completion, reminders, revisions, and countersignatures; maintain correctly named, access-controlled final agreements and a reliable central TA document repository.
* ATS Data Integrity. Maintain accurate offer-stage information, key dates, approvals, document status, and supporting records in ATS. Audit records for completeness, promptly resolve discrepancies, and support trustworthy operational reporting.
* Cross-functional Coordination. Partner with recruiters, practice/operations leaders, Legal, HR, Credentialing, and other stakeholders to reconcile start dates, contracting updates, document changes, and time-sensitive handoffs. Track open items through closure and communicate status and ownership.
* Attestations and Risk Escalation. Manage collection, tracking, and follow-up of required candidate attestations and related disclosures. Identify missing, inconsistent, or potentially concerning information and promptly escalate it to designated Legal, Compliance, or other decisionmakers without making independent legal or eligibility determinations.
* Process Improvement. Maintain checklists, standard work, queue visibility, and issue logs. Recommend improvements that reduce errors, rework, avoidable delays, and candidate confusion while preserving necessary approval controls.

QUALIFICATIONS & EXPERIENCE

Required

* At least 2 years of relevant experience in high-accuracy document administration, offer or contract coordination, recruiting operations, HR operations, or a comparable controlled-workflow function.
* Demonstrated ability to review complex, detail-sensitive documents for consistency and completeness and manage multiple concurrent transactions with firm deadlines.
* Strong business writing, stakeholder follow-up, confidentiality, and proficiency with Microsoft Office, electronic document systems, and shared records.
* Associate’s or bachelor’s degree preferred; equivalent relevant experience accepted.

Preferred

* 3+ years of relevant experience, particularly in provider recruiting, healthcare workforce operations, contract administration, or offer management.
* Experience in a paralegal, legal assistant, or contract-coordinator environment, with a clear understanding of administrative versus legal decision-making responsibilities.
* Working knowledge of ATS; experience with DocuSign/Adobe Sign or equivalent eSignature and platforms.
* Experience with clinical employment documentation, approvals, and sensitive candidate disclosures.

CORE CAPABILITIES

Exceptional attention to detail; structured organization; proactive issue escalation; sound judgment; strong service orientation; comfort working across Recruiting, Legal, HR, and Operations; ability to maintain control without creating unnecessary delays.

MEASURES OF SUCCESS

* Offer document accuracy and first-pass completion rate; frequency of preventable corrections or rework.
* Turnaround time from approved terms to document release and from release to full execution.
* Completeness and timeliness of Greenhouse records, final-file retention, and attestation follow-up.
* Aging of outstanding approvals, signatures, and escalated issues; quality of stakeholder communication.

ROLE BOUNDARIES & DECISION RIGHTS

The coordinator executes approved processes and highlights variances. Recruiters and designated business approvers own commercial offer terms; Legal and Compliance own legal interpretation, risk adjudication, and approval of contract language.

GENERAL EXPECTATIONS

Deliver accurate work on deadline; protect confidential information; communicate professionally; collaborate across teams; maintain reliable records; escalate issues promptly; and support continuous improvement. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable qualified individuals to perform essential functions.

Work environment: Professional, computer-based role involving telephone/video communication and routine use of office equipment. Final physical requirements and job classification are subject to HR review.

ed69239871aff84fb6cb.title: Clinical TA Intake Coordinator
ed69239871aff84fb6cb.description:
POSITION PURPOSE

The Clinical TA Intake Coordinator serves as the first response and scheduling hub for inbound clinical applicants. This role converts timely, professional outreach into completed recruiter screening appointments, ensures accurate candidate routing and ATS records, and strengthens intake quality by identifying avoidable process-related rejections. The coordinator supports recruiter productivity through speed, responsiveness, disciplined follow-up, and a consistent candidate experience.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

* Candidate Experience and Conversion. Manage incoming applications and assigned leads; make prompt, personalized contact within TA-established response standards using approved phone, email, and text channels.
* Direct Recruiter Scheduling. Identify the appropriate recruiter; coordinate candidate availability and schedule screening appointments directly on recruiter calendars. Confirm time zones, send clear meeting details, and manage rescheduling and missed-appointment follow-up.
* Initial Intake and Routing. Collect limited, standardized intake information needed for efficient recruiter engagement; confirm basic nonclinical details, identify duplicates, document candidate preferences, and flag questions for recruiter review.
* APP, RT, and CRNA Triage. Prioritize inbound applicants (Advanced Practice Provider, Radiation Therapist, and CRNA) and schedule recruiter screens as capacity and defined workflows permit. Apply differentiated response expectations so these populations do not displace the physician service standard.
* Rejection-Reason Quality Control. Audit pre-presentation dispositions and rejection reasons for completeness, consistent categorization, and process accuracy. Surface recurring patterns and potential missed engagement opportunities to recruiters and leadership; request corrections through the established review process.
* Candidate Experience and ATS Integrity. Maintain clear, professional candidate communication and accurate Greenhouse activities, stages, contact attempts, notes, routing, and appointments. Close the loop on inquiries and handoffs so applicants are not lost between intake and recruiter review.
* Reporting and Department Projects. Track contact, scheduling, show-rate, and intake quality measures. Support TA process-improvement and special projects when coverage permits, with physician intake responsiveness remaining the first priority.

QUALIFICATIONS & EXPERIENCE

Required

* At least 1 year of relevant experience in inside sales, high-volume recruiting or recruiting coordination, candidate engagement, customer success, contact-center operations, or high-volume appointment scheduling.
* Demonstrated success with time-sensitive follow-up, professional phone communication, multi-channel outreach, and scheduling across multiple calendars.
* Ability to navigate high volumes of competing requests while maintaining accurate records, confidentiality, and a positive customer or candidate experience.
* Strong proficiency with Microsoft Outlook/calendar tools and basic Microsoft Office applications; degree not required when relevant experience is demonstrated.

Preferred

* 2–3 years of experience in high-volume recruiting, sales/ sales development, healthcare recruitment support, medical office intake, or a comparable service-intensive role.
* Experience with ATS / CRM system(s), including stage updates, contact logging, workflow queues, and reports.
* Evidence of performance against response-time, appointment-setting, conversion, attendance, or service-quality targets.
* Familiarity with physician, APP, Radiation Therapist, or CRNA recruiting workflows, or demonstrated ability to learn specialist terminology quickly.

CORE CAPABILITIES

Urgency with accuracy; strong phone and written communication; consultative questioning; respectful persistence; disciplined scheduling; excellent candidate service; comfort with performance metrics and coaching.

MEASURES OF SUCCESS

* Physician time-to-first-attempt, time-to-live-contact, and percentage reached within established response standards.
* Qualified inbound leads converted to booked recruiter screens; scheduling turnaround and screen attendance/show rate.
* Accuracy and completeness of intake and rejection-reason dispositions; minimize pre-presentation process losses.
* ATS record accuracy, handoff completeness, and adherence to physician-priority routing expectations.

ROLE BOUNDARIES & DECISION RIGHTS

The coordinator owns outreach, routing, scheduling, intake documentation, and reason-code audits. Recruiters own substantive qualification, presentation, and rejection decisions. The coordinator must not change disposition decisions to improve metrics.

GENERAL EXPECTATIONS

Deliver accurate work on deadline; protect confidential information; communicate professionally; collaborate across teams; maintain reliable records; escalate issues promptly; and support continuous improvement. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable qualified individuals to perform essential functions.

Work environment: Professional, computer-based role involving telephone/video communication and routine use of office equipment. Final physical requirements and job classification are subject to HR review.

**Location:** Remote (U.S.)

**Type:** Full-Time

About Autism Learning Partners

Autism Learning Partners (ALP) is a leading provider of autism and developmental disability services. We are committed to helping children and families achieve meaningful progress through compassionate, high-quality care.

About the Role

Autism Learning Partners is seeking a **Clinician Workforce Operations Specialist** to own the systems, processes, and operational accuracy behind our clinician recruiting efforts.

This hands-on role combines backend ATS administration, recruiting operations, data validation, and continuous process improvement. You'll manage and optimize Paradox workflows, maintain accurate requisition and pipeline data, validate reporting dashboards, and independently troubleshoot operational challenges.

We're looking for someone who brings strong technical skills, exceptional attention to detail, and a track record of turning operational challenges into practical, lasting improvements. This is an individual contributor role with significant ownership and the opportunity to make a measurable impact across our clinician recruiting team.

What You'll Do

**Recruiting Systems & ATS Administration**

* Own backend administration of Paradox, including system configurations, workflows, automations, permissions, templates, and ongoing maintenance.
* Independently configure, test, troubleshoot, and implement approved system changes, including requisition, candidate, and offer-related workflows.
* Partner with internal stakeholders and system vendors to resolve technical issues, optimize system functionality, and improve the recruiter and candidate experience.

**Recruiting Operations & Data Integrity**

* Manage daily clinician recruiting operations, including requisition updates, job postings, and maintenance of the Clinical Recruiting Breakdown (CRB).
* Maintain accurate candidate pipeline data, recruiting records, and operational trackers, including stages, dispositions, and candidate aging.
* Own ongoing maintenance and validation of existing Databricks dashboards, partnering with analytics on technical fixes.
* Reconcile data across Paradox, the CRB, Excel, and reporting tools to identify discrepancies and ensure accurate leadership reporting.

**Operational Audits & Continuous Improvement**

* Conduct recurring audits of requisitions, job postings, recruiting data, and workflows to identify risks and process-compliance gaps.
* Independently investigate operational challenges, recommend solutions, and implement approved improvements from testing through rollout.
* Develop and maintain SOPs, checklists, trackers, and training resources, leveraging technology and approved AI tools to improve efficiency.
* Partner with recruiting leadership and the BT Talent Acquisition Operations Specialist to align processes, reporting standards, and cross-team coverage.

What We're Looking For

* **3+ years of experience** in Talent Acquisition, recruiting operations, or ATS administration.
* **Demonstrated experience independently configuring, testing, troubleshooting, and maintaining ATS workflows, automations, permissions, and system settings.**
* **Advanced Excel proficiency**, including XLOOKUP or comparable formulas, PivotTables, data validation, and reconciliation.
* Experience validating and interpreting dashboards using Databricks, Power BI, Tableau, or similar tools. SQL is not required.
* Proven experience conducting operational audits, developing SOPs, and implementing process improvements.
* Strong analytical and troubleshooting skills, with the ability to identify issues, recommend solutions, and follow through independently.
* Exceptional attention to detail, organization, accountability, and communication skills.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience with Paradox (Olivia) or administration of a comparable ATS.
* Experience in healthcare, ABA, behavioral health, or multi-site recruiting operations.
* Experience supporting ATS implementations, system configurations, or workflow testing.
* Familiarity with Databricks, Power BI, or basic SQL.
* Bachelor's degree in a related field preferred but not required.

Why This Role Matters

Behind every successful clinician hire is an operation that needs to run smoothly. This role ensures our recruiting team has accurate information, reliable systems, and efficient processes to bring qualified clinicians to the children and families who need them.

**If you're someone who sees a problem, finds a solution, and takes pride in making things work better, we'd love to hear from you!**

***Join Immatics and shape*** ***the future*** ***of cancer immunotherapy;*** ***one patient at a time!***

Immatics is committed to making a meaningful impact on the lives of patients with cancer. We are the global leader in precision targeting of **PRAME**, a target expressed in more than 50 cancers. Our cutting-edge science and robust clinical pipeline form the broadest **PRAME** franchise with the most **PRAME** indications and modalities, spanning TCR T-cell therapies and TCR bispecifics.

**Why Join Us?**

* **Innovative Environment:** Help to pioneer advancements in cancer immunotherapy.
* **Collaborative Culture:** Be part of a diverse team dedicated to your professional growth.
* **Global Impact:** Contribute to therapies that make a lasting impact on patients globally.

**Role Overview**

The **Director, Team Lead, Site Operations** is the formal people leader and functional process owner for assigned Site Operations personnel within Clinical Operations. The role is accountable for line management, resource planning, capability development, functional quality, and the design, maintenance, and continuous improvement of designated Site Operations and Clinical Operations processes. The Team Lead enables consistent, compliant execution across Germany and the United States and partners closely with Clinical Operations Leads to ensure appropriately skilled resources are assigned to studies.

**Reports to:** Executive Director, Clinical Operations

**Location:** Remote

**Basic Qualifications:**

* Bachelor's degree in Life Sciences, Pharmacy, Nursing, or a related discipline required.
* 10+ years of experience in Clinical Operations or related functions within biotech or pharmaceutical industries, with 5+ years of that experience in direct people leadership, managing clinical operations professionals

**Preferred Qualifications:**

* Master's degree in Life Sciences, Pharmacy, Nursing, or a related discipline
* 5+ years of clinical monitoring experience within the pharmaceutical or biotechnology industry, including roles as a Clinical Research Associate and/or Clinical Trial Manager.
* Demonstrated late phase experience in oncology.
* Experience in cell therapy or other complex investigational therapies strongly preferred.
* Strong working knowledge of ICH-GCP, FDA regulations, and global clinical trial requirements.
* Demonstrated ability to lead cross-functional initiatives and influence stakeholders across multiple organizational levels.
* Proven experience managing resources, priorities, and competing business demands in a dynamic environment.
* History of driving operational improvements and implementing innovative approaches within Clinical Operations.
* Experience supporting regulatory inspections and audit readiness activities.

**In** **this Role You Will:**

People Leadership and Talent Development

* Serve as the formal line manager for assigned Site Operations personnel, including Clinical Trial Associates, Clinical Research Associates and Clinical Trial Managers, and other roles as assigned.
* Recruit, onboard, coach, develop, and retain team members who meet role requirements and contribute to a high-performing, collaborative Clinical Operations culture.
* Set individual objectives, provide regular and meaningful performance feedback, conduct formal performance evaluations, and support career development, succession planning, and promotion readiness.
* Create an environment of trust, accountability, inclusion, and psychological safety while addressing performance or conduct concerns promptly and appropriately.
* Ensure team members maintain the training, qualifications, competencies, and functional knowledge required for their assigned responsibilities.
* Partner with the Clinical Operations Leads (COLs) to ensure study roles, priorities, timelines and deliverables are clear, serving as a point of escalation and receive study-performance feedback on team members.

Resource and Capacity Management

* Maintain visibility of team capacity, capabilities, workload, and development needs; lead resource forecasting and cross-study workload balancing in consultation with the Head of Clinical Operations.
* Assign or reassign Site Operations personnel to studies based on portfolio priorities, required competencies, workload, continuity needs, and development opportunities, in consultation with the relevant Clinical Operations Leads.
* Identify current and future capacity gaps and recommend hiring, contractor support, capability development, or other resource solutions.

Functional Process Ownership and Operational Excellence

* Own, develop, maintain, and harmonize designated Site Operations and Clinical Operations processes, SOPs, work instructions, guidance documents, templates, and training materials in partnership with relevant stakeholders and Quality.
* Ensure consistent implementation of applicable Clinical Operations processes and standards across studies and regions while accommodating appropriate local requirements in Germany and the United States.
* Drive continuous improvement and global harmonization through review of lessons learned, recurring issues, metrics, audit and inspection observations, CAPAs, and user feedback.
* Establish and monitor functional metrics and key performance indicators relevant to Site Operations, resource utilization, process quality, and organizational effectiveness; identify trends and implement improvement actions as appropriate.
* Support organizational change, technology adoption, and process improvements that increase quality, consistency, scalability, and efficiency across Clinical Operations.

Quality, Compliance, and Site Operations Expertise

* Maintain expert-level knowledge of ICH GCP, applicable regulations, clinical monitoring practices, and evolving industry expectations relevant to Site Operations.
* Support functional inspection and audit readiness, including preparation of personnel, processes, documentation, and evidence of oversight; coordinate corrective and preventive actions within the function as assigned.
* Provide subject matter expertise for site management, clinical monitoring, monitoring strategy, oversight models, and related Site Operations processes without assuming accountability for day-to-day delivery of individual clinical trials.
* Collaborate with Clinical Operations Leads and cross-functional partners to identify systemic risks, process gaps, and capability needs that may affect multiple studies or the Clinical Operations portfolio.
* Model transparent communication, reliable execution, sound judgment, and collaborative leadership across the global Clinical Operations organization.

**Qualified candidates** **will participate in** **a structured interview process, which includes:**

* An initial recruiter phone screen (conducted via video)
* A recruiter-facilitated introduction and interview with the hiring leader and key stakeholders (via video)
* A final-stage interview, which may include an in-person meeting at our U.S. Headquarters in Houston, TX

**What do we offer?**

At Immatics, we believe in investing in our team’s health, safety and well-being. Here’s what you can expect if you join Immatics:

**Comprehensive Benefits:**

* Competitive rates for Health, Dental, and Vision Insurance
* 4 weeks of vacation, granted up front each year and prorated for first and last year of employment.
* 12 company paid holidays
* 7 days of sick time
* 100% employer-paid life insurance up to at 1x annual salary, up to one hundred thousand dollars
* 100% employer-paid short- and long-Term disability coverage

* The company will match 100% of your contributions up to 3% of your base salary for the first two years of employment, 4% for years 2-3 of employment, and up to 5% of your salary from the fourth year onward of continued employment.
* Partially paid parental leave for eligible employees.
Additional voluntary employee-paid benefits and services, including accident, hospital indemnity, and critical illness insurance, as well as identity theft protection and pet insurance.  

  
  

**Equal Employment Opportunity**

We are an equal opportunity employer and are committed to building a diverse and inclusive workplace. We consider all qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, ancestry, age, marital status, disability, genetic information, veteran status, or any other status protected by applicable law.

**Reasonable Accommodations**

If you require assistance or accommodation during the application or interview process, please contact us at RecruitingUS@immatics.com.

**Pre-Employment Requirements**

Employment is contingent upon successful completion of a background check, reference checks and pre-employment drug screening, where permitted by applicable law. For certain roles, additional screenings such as a credit check or motor vehicle record review may be required, where job-related and consistent with business necessity.

409c6ddeef8f654d70da.description:
**About the Role:**

As a CBRE Operations Management Sr. Director, you will oversee the department responsible for planning, managing, and directing business operations for a large region or high-profile client.

This job is part of the Operations Management job function. They are responsible for coordinating staff functions and operations that support the organization’s goals and strategies.

* Provide formal supervision to employees. Monitor the training and development of staff. Conduct performance evaluations and coaching. Oversee the recruiting and hiring of new employees.
* Coordinate and manage the team's daily activities. Establish work schedules, assign tasks, and cross-train staff. Set and track staff and department deadlines. Mentor and coach as needed.

At TISTA, you’ll do meaningful, mission-driven work that improves lives alongside teammates you trust and leaders who are transparent and supportive. We invest in your learning and internal mobility so you can build a career that keeps advancing. We’re proud to serve and hire Veterans, and we put people first in everything we do.

3cc52f5d0f40d7d2c033.description:
**On-Site Location:** Nephrology & Hypertension Associates, 370 Middletown Boulevard, #504, Langhorne, PA 19047

Are you looking for a role that:

* You can earn above average income based on work ethic and efficiency?
* Is a hybrid position allowing work from home opportunities?
* Is less stressful than a typical hands-on healthcare job? (Not on your feet, mostly desk work).
* Offers promotion opportunities at an aggressively growing company?
* Provides all the training and support you need to be successful

If so, we are hiring for CMA, CCMA, or LPN's. The role involves onboarding patients into our VCM (Virtual Care Management) program, and performing patient monitoring activities. This is a hybrid opportunity: you must be able to work on-site at Nephrology & Hypertension Associates (370 Middletown Boulevard, #504, Langhorne, PA 19047) for 8 hours a day at least 3 days a week, with the remaining time worked remotely. We are looking for people who can commit to 25 to 40 hours a week and who live no more than a 30-minute commute from this location.

Vironix Health is one the fastest growing Ai-health technology companies across the globe with cutting edge virtual care management (VCM) technologies that provide invaluable preventative care to patients with coronary, respiratory, and kidney diseases. Our comprehensive, flagship product provides Remote Physiologic Monitoring (RPM), and Complex Chronic Care Management (CCCM) services to physician practices for enhanced patient care and significant new revenue generation. We further provide cellular-enabled devices, software, mobile apps, and monitoring staff to support patients and improve outcomes while reducing healthcare costs and hospitalizations.

How You Get Paid — 3 Buckets

Contractors earn $24–$32/hour on average. Top MAs can earn as much as $40/hour. Monthly paychecks typically range from $3,000–$7,000/month.

Bucket 1 – Remote Patient Monitoring (70–95% of pay)

* Conduct scheduled virtual check-ins with patients (weekly or monthly) to follow up on symptoms and medications
* Respond to software alerts when vital sign anomalies are detected (e.g., dangerously high blood pressure)
* Can be done from home (8 AM–5 PM) or on-site

Bucket 2 – Patient Enrollment (On-Site) | $15 per enrolled patient

* Be present at the doctor's office at least 3 days/week to enroll patients in the RPM program
* When a patient comes in, you have ~10 minutes to introduce the program and walk them through enrollment
* Real-time access to the patient schedule — you always know what your day looks like
* Submit your preferred on-site days weeks in advance (3–5 days); the team schedules around your availability

Bucket 3 – On-Site Hourly Base | $7.25/hour

* Clock in/out during on-site hours — covers commute time and gas
* During downtime between enrollments, continue remote monitoring from a dedicated contractor station — earning from all 3 buckets simultaneously

Requirements

* CMA, CCMA or LPN Certification / License
* Medical Assisting and Patient Care skills
* Knowledge of Medical Terminology
* Experience in Medical Office procedures
* Experience in taking vital sign and weight measures
* Proficiency in managing Medical Records
* Excellent communication and interpersonal skills

aa6d2a45b022b4aa6b83.description:
**About Affinity eHealth**

Affinity eHealth is a leading Third-Party Administrator (TPA) of drug and alcohol testing services, specializing in the Professional Health Monitoring market. We support professional monitoring programs across North America, providing comprehensive testing administration, collection site management, and technology solutions that help programs effectively monitor participant compliance.

Central to our operations is an extensive North American network of specimen collection sites that provides convenient, reliable, and professional collection services to individuals participating in monitoring programs.

**Position Overview**

Affinity eHealth is seeking a **Collection Site Coordinator** to join our Customer Care team.

Reporting to the Manager of Customer Care, the Collection Site Coordinator will play a key role in the ongoing management, development, and optimization of Affinity's collection site network.

The successful candidate will be responsible for establishing and maintaining relationships with collection site providers, expanding network coverage, negotiating pricing, coordinating collection procedures, and resolving operational issues.

This position requires strong organizational, communication, negotiation, and problem-solving skills, together with an understanding of specimen collection procedures and the operational requirements of drug and alcohol testing programs.

**Key Responsibilities**

**Collection Site Network Management & Development**

* Support the day-to-day management and administration of Affinity's North American collection site network.
* Identify, evaluate, and recruit new collection sites to expand network coverage and address geographic service gaps.
* Maintain relationships with existing collection site providers, including independent collection facilities and larger national and regional provider organizations.
* Negotiate collection service pricing, fee schedules, and service arrangements with providers to ensure competitive pricing and cost-effective network operations.
* Monitor collection site availability, geographic coverage, service capabilities, and performance to ensure the network continues to meet client and participant needs.
* Manage relationships and operational activities involving FormFox Marketplace, and other third-party collection site networks.
* Identify opportunities to improve network accessibility, efficiency, and service quality.

**Collection Protocols, Training & Quality Assurance**

* Develop, document, and maintain collection protocols and procedural instructions specific to Affinity's client and program requirements.
* Communicate collection requirements to participating sites and provide training and guidance on applicable procedures.
* Ensure collection sites understand and follow the appropriate specimen collection, documentation, chain-of-custody, and specimen shipping procedures.
* Coordinate with collection sites to address procedural deficiencies, collection errors, and other service quality concerns.
* Assist in the investigation and resolution of collection-related incidents, participant complaints, and operational issues.
* Support continuous improvement initiatives to strengthen collection site reliability, consistency, and service quality.

**Operational Support & Coordination**

* Work closely with Affinity's Customer Care and Account Management teams to address collection site requirements and resolve client or participant service issues.
* Assist in identifying suitable collection locations for participants with specific geographic, scheduling, or collection requirements.
* Coordinate with collection site providers to resolve issues involving missed collections, site availability, collection procedures, and service disruptions.
* Support the Finance team in researching and resolving collection site invoicing, billing discrepancies, payment inquiries, and pricing issues.
* Maintain accurate and current collection site information within Affinity's proprietary SPECTRUM platform, including contact information, locations, operating hours, collection capabilities, negotiated pricing, and other operational details.
* Prepare and maintain network-related documentation, provider records, and operational reports.
* Collaborate with internal teams to identify process improvements and opportunities to enhance the overall collection site experience for clients and participants.

**Qualifications & Experience**

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Previous experience in the drug and alcohol testing industry, particularly in collection site network management, specimen collection operations, or Third-Party Administration.
* Familiarity with urine, oral fluid, hair, and other specimen collection methods and associated chain-of-custody procedures.
* Experience working with national or regional specimen collection providers, laboratories, or collection site management networks.
* Knowledge of both regulated and non-regulated drug testing environments, including the distinct requirements of professional monitoring programs.
* Experience negotiating pricing, managing vendor relationships, or coordinating service provider networks.
* Familiarity with collection management platforms, including FormFox or similar systems, would be an asset.

**Required Skills & Competencies**

* Strong interpersonal and relationship management skills, with the ability to establish effective working relationships with external providers and internal teams.
* Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
* Strong organizational abilities, attention to detail, and the capacity to manage multiple priorities simultaneously.
* Effective negotiation and problem-solving skills.
* A proactive, resourceful, and customer-service-oriented approach.
* Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively within a team.
* Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications and the ability to learn proprietary software and database systems.
* Sound judgment and professionalism when handling sensitive information and resolving service-related issues.

**Why Join Affinity eHealth?**

Affinity eHealth operates in a specialized and growing industry, providing essential services that support professional accountability, public safety, and the successful participation of individuals in professional monitoring programs.

As a Collection Site Coordinator, you will have the opportunity to:

* Play a meaningful role in the development and management of an extensive North American collection network.
* Build relationships with a diverse range of collection providers and industry partners.
* Contribute directly to improvements in network efficiency, accessibility, and service quality.
* Work collaboratively with an experienced team in a specialized healthcare services environment.
* Help strengthen the infrastructure that supports Affinity's continued growth and commitment to client service.

**How to Apply**

Interested candidates are invited to submit their résumé and a brief cover letter outlining their relevant experience, particularly in specimen collection operations, collection network management, or drug and alcohol testing services.

Affinity eHealth is an equal opportunity employer committed to providing an inclusive and respectful workplace.

Pay: $40,000.00 - $60,000.00 per year

Work Location: Remote
